title: kbmon --status answers sessions, cost, query log and coord questions in plain words from one snapshot
goal: kbmon.py --status [TOPIC] prints a short plain-words answer for TOPIC (sessions, cost, querylog, coord, sprints, load or all, all by default) from one snapshot of the panels the topic needs, built in a new _tools/mon_status.py, also from --from-snapshot; --status TOPIC --json prints an object with schema 1, topic, taken, lines and facts; sessions names each orphan by pid and age and each stalled item by id with its signals, pointing to kbask.py summary for why; cost gives today's dollars, usage rows, tokens and each unpriced model from the querylog panel's usage_today; querylog gives the last delivery outcome and the undelivered count; coord gives each live claim's key, time left and budget, never its holder; every line passes redact.redact and names no path outside the clone; an answer is at most 25 lines; it calls no model and writes no file

clauses.clause: kbmon.py --status [TOPIC] prints a short plain-words answer for TOPIC (sessions, cost, querylog, coord, sprints, load or all, all by default) from one snapshot of the panels the topic needs, built in a new _tools/mon_status.py, also from --from-snapshot
--status TOPIC --json prints an object with schema 1, topic, taken, lines and facts
sessions names each orphan by pid and age and each stalled item by id with its signals, pointing to kbask.py summary for why
cost gives today's dollars, usage rows, tokens and each unpriced model from the querylog panel's usage_today
querylog gives the last delivery outcome and the undelivered count
coord gives each live claim's key, time left and budget, never its holder
every line passes redact.redact and names no path outside the clone
an answer is at most 25 lines
it calls no model and writes no file

gates.question: How does a status answer speak? The operator's rule: "speak results, not backlog ids".
options: results in plain words with real numbers, an item by its title, an id only on a line where the operator acts (a gate to answer, an item to release)
title and id together on every item, as the sprint skill names items
ids and counts only, no titles
gates.recommendation: results in plain words with real numbers, an item by its title, an id only on a line where the operator acts (a gate to answer, an item to release)
gates.answer: results in plain words with real numbers, an item by its title, an id only on a line where the operator acts (a gate to answer, an item to release)

gates.question: What exit code does kbmon.py --status return when the snapshot has an alert?
options: 0 always: the answer is shown, an alert is its content
1 when the snapshot has an alert, as --once and --json do
gates.recommendation: 0 always: the answer is shown, an alert is its content
gates.answer: 0 always: the answer is shown, an alert is its content

gates.question: Which panels does the load topic read, and how does all bound its length?
options: load reads host and sessions; all gives each topic four lines and a pointer to --status TOPIC when it holds more
load reads host only; all prints each topic in full and cuts the whole at 25 lines
gates.recommendation: load reads host and sessions; all gives each topic four lines and a pointer to --status TOPIC when it holds more
gates.answer: load reads host and sessions; all gives each topic four lines and a pointer to --status TOPIC when it holds more

gates.question: Where does a status line get an item's title?
options: from the clone's own backlog (--root), the id alone for an item it does not hold, so a saved snapshot still answers
from the snapshot only, ids everywhere
gates.recommendation: from the clone's own backlog (--root), the id alone for an item it does not hold, so a saved snapshot still answers
gates.answer: from the clone's own backlog (--root), the id alone for an item it does not hold, so a saved snapshot still answers

notes: Plan 2026-10-19: premise on the base: kbmon.py --status cost exits 2 (unrecognized arguments); the planted snapshot renders with --once --from-snapshot (exit 1 on its orphan alert), so the check fails only on --status. Frozen operator questions: 'status and percentage of done on sprints', 'check what causes high load on my computer', 'which sessions are running / is anything stuck or orphaned', 'how much did today cost', 'did the query log deliver', 'what is left before X is done'. The coord panel's own text view prints the holder; the status answer must not. The sprints and load topics render the panel data there today; ST-db4gscgj and ST-tdypjvev extend them. A topic runs only the panels it needs, each under kbmon's --timeout.
